105: He plucks the small ones - there are those stunted onions that will never grow large, which are called TzIB"S in a foreign language. They are uprooted from among the large ones to make more space for them to spread out. Now these would be placed into the owner's vessels, and would not be excluded [from that produce which a worker is allowed to eat] by "but you shall not put any in your vessel" [Deuteronomy 23:25], but must instead be excluded by "threshing". [The plucking of the small garlic and onions] is not during the time of the completion of their work; the main point of this activity is to improve the growth [of the non-stunted onions] since they remain attached [to the ground].
